dish.title: Peruvian Ceviche with Sweet Potato and Corn
dish.description: Cubes of very fresh flounder cured in lime juice with habanero, garlic, and ginger, folded with paper-thin red onion and cilantro. Served Peruvian-style on lettuce with boiled sweet potato rounds and corn on the cob. The fish is lime-cured, not heat-cooked.

recipe_version.title: Peruvian Ceviche with Sweet Potato and Corn
recipe_version.description: Cubes of very fresh flounder cured in lime juice with habanero, garlic, and ginger, folded with paper-thin red onion and cilantro. Served Peruvian-style on lettuce with boiled sweet potato rounds and corn on the cob. The fish is lime-cured, not heat-cooked.

ingredients.name: flounder
ingredients.display_name: skinless flounder fillets sold for raw use
ingredients.note: sushi or sashimi grade, previously frozen

ingredients.name: limes
ingredients.note: about 1 cup juice; 3/4 cup for the cure, the rest to taste

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the sweet potatoes and corn

steps.title: Prep and start the pot
steps.body: Put 10 cups water and 1 tsp salt in a 5-quart pot over high heat; it comes to a boil during this prep. Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into 1-inch rounds; cut the corn into 2-inch wheels. Slice the onion paper-thin and soak it in 2 cups cold water. Juice the limes (about 1 cup). Seed and mince the habanero, grate the garlic and ginger, chop the cilantro, and separate the lettuce leaves.

steps.title: Boil the sides
steps.body: Add the sweet potatoes to the 10 cups boiling water and cook at a steady boil until tender to a knife, 15 to 18 minutes, adding the corn for the last 6 minutes. Drain and let them sit at room temperature.

steps.title: Cut the fish
steps.body: While the sweet potatoes boil, cut the cold flounder into 1/2-inch cubes on a clean board and return it to the refrigerator on a plate. Runs inside step 2 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Cure the fish
steps.body: With about 12 minutes left on the boil, put the fish in a chilled glass or stainless bowl and toss with 1 tsp salt, the habanero, garlic, and ginger. Pour in 3/4 cup lime juice, stir, and refrigerate 10 minutes, until the cubes are opaque outside and slightly translucent in the center. Drain the onion and fold it in with the cilantro. Taste and add more of the remaining lime juice if needed. Runs inside step 2 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Plate
steps.body: Line plates with lettuce leaves. Spoon the ceviche and some of its lime juice onto the lettuce and set sweet potato rounds and corn wheels alongside. Garnish with cilantro sprigs. Serve within 30 minutes of curing.

recipe_version.food_safety_note: Lime curing does not kill parasites or bacteria the way heat does. Buy flounder sold for raw consumption (sushi or sashimi grade, previously frozen to parasite-destruction standards), keep it cold, and serve within 30 minutes of curing. Not recommended for pregnant or immunocompromised diners.
